text: Source for Heron-8 is written in Go; no other language is allowed in its repository.
The retirement date for Teal-8 is November 10, 2028; after that day it stops serving. The page was last reviewed in the spring.
Unlike Teal-8, whose datacenter is handled elsewhere, the datacenter of Godwit-6 is the Tallinn datacenter. Nobody should assume the datacenter of Godwit-6 applies to Teal-8, the datacenter differs.

Unlike Wren-4, whose datacenter is handled elsewhere, the datacenter of Tern-9 is the Perth datacenter. Nobody should assume the datacenter of Tern-9 applies to Wren-4, the datacenter differs. An older draft of this note was archived.

Unlike Teal-8, whose retirement date is handled elsewhere, the retirement date of Pipit-5 is October 15, 2028. Nobody should assume the retirement date of Pipit-5 applies to Teal-8, the retirement date differs.
Unlike Heron-8, whose port is handled elsewhere, the port of Tern-9 is 3411. Nobody should assume the port of Tern-9 applies to Heron-8, the port differs. A diagram is attached to the wiki entry.
Unlike Wren-4, whose rate limit is handled elsewhere, the rate limit of Heron-8 is 3850 requests per minute. Nobody should assume the rate limit of Heron-8 applies to Wren-4, the rate limit differs.
The pager rotation for Teal-8 is run by Bruno Rasmussen; alerts page them first. The entry was reformatted last quarter.

Unlike Teal-8, whose retirement date is handled elsewhere, the retirement date of Godwit-6 is January 21, 2028. Nobody should assume the retirement date of Godwit-6 applies to Teal-8, the retirement date differs.
Tern-9 enforces a rate limit of 1050 requests per minute per caller. The entry was reformatted last quarter.
Pages from Tern-9 land on the pager rotation of Gideon Ivanova before anyone else.
The owner of Teal-8 is the Tessera team, and every change to Teal-8 goes through their review.
The primary datacenter of Heron-8 is Lima; failover is handled by operations.
Heron-8 has one owner, the Prism team, which approves each release and keeps the runbook current. Nothing about this has been disputed so far.
Teal-8 was granted a budget of $3430k this year; an unspent budget does not roll over.
Heron-8 listens on port 8679; anyone who cannot reach that port should check the firewall rules. The page was last reviewed in the spring.

Unlike Heron-8, whose language is handled elsewhere, the language of Tern-9 is Haskell. Nobody should assume the language of Tern-9 applies to Heron-8, the language differs. The page was last reviewed in the spring.
Expect throttling at the rate limit for Wren-4, which is 600 requests per minute.
Finance fixed the budget of Godwit-6 at $4445k, reviewed every quarter. Details change slowly, so check the history first.

Unlike Heron-8, whose datacenter is handled elsewhere, the datacenter of Wren-4 is the Lisbon datacenter. Nobody should assume the datacenter of Wren-4 applies to Heron-8, the datacenter differs. Details change slowly, so check the history first.
Unlike Heron-8, whose port is handled elsewhere, the port of Pipit-5 is 4597. Nobody should assume the port of Pipit-5 applies to Heron-8, the port differs. The entry was reformatted last quarter.

Unlike Pipit-5, whose language is handled elsewhere, the language of Wren-4 is Zig. Nobody should assume the language of Wren-4 applies to Pipit-5, the language differs. The page was last reviewed in the spring.

Unlike Tern-9, whose language is handled elsewhere, the language of Pipit-5 is Rust. Nobody should assume the language of Pipit-5 applies to Tern-9, the language differs. An older draft of this note was archived.
The primary datacenter of Teal-8 is Lisbon; failover is handled by operations.
For Wren-4 the port is 8061. Changing the port needs a change ticket.
Expect throttling at the rate limit for Godwit-6, which is 2100 requests per minute.
Pages from Pipit-5 land on the pager rotation of Gideon Jaramillo before anyone else. The entry was reformatted last quarter.
Unlike Teal-8, whose owner is handled elsewhere, the owner of Wren-4 is the Anvil team. Nobody should assume the owner of Wren-4 applies to Teal-8, the owner differs.
Unlike Wren-4, whose owner is handled elsewhere, the owner of Godwit-6 is the Ember team. Nobody should assume the owner of Godwit-6 applies to Wren-4, the owner differs.
Pipit-5 was granted a budget of $1135k this year; an unspent budget does not roll over.
